claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is/are the child/children you're claiming for?** 

Please tell me their age or age range:
- **Under 16 years old?**
- **16 to 19 years old?** (in education or training)
- **20 years old or over?**

Also, please share the **names** of all the children you're inquiring about, as I'll need these for the final assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex, who is 13 years old**. That's great - at 13, Alex falls into the under 16 category, which is a good starting point.

Let me continue with the eligibility check by navigating through the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(This is mainly relevant for children aged 16 and over, but I need to verify this for completeness in the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is still in school and not working, so that's a positive factor. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, **is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** Specifically, is he NOT receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit in his own right?

(Since he's 13 and in school, he likely isn't receiving these, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - this next check is about apprenticeships. **Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's 13 and in school, I suspect the answer is no, but I need to confirm to be thorough.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just at regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular school and not in an apprenticeship. Let me proceed to the next stage:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several possible paths to meeting UK residency requirements for Child Benefit:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK?**
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work, OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family (and not claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit), OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries?**

Which, if any, of these apply to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check: **Are you responsible for Alex?** This means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. - could be weekly, monthly, or lump sum payments), OR
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement** that covers Alex's upkeep and equals or exceeds the Child Benefit payment?

Which of these apply to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is another family member or guardian claiming for him?

Or are you the only person who would be claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're the only claimant. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check: **Where is Alex currently living?** Specifically:

- **Is he currently in hospital?**
- **Is he in local authority care?**
- **Is he being fostered?**
- **Or is he living at home normally** (which I think is the case based on what you've said)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living at home normally with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home normally with you. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final check: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you covering Alex's costs yourself without the council paying for his accommodation or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm covering everything myself - the council isn't paying anything towards him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! That's excellent news. You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me now provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

Congratulations! You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for your 13-year-old son, Alex.

---

### **Why You're Eligible:**
- ✅ Alex is under 16 (a qualifying age)
- ✅ He's in school (not working full-time)
- ✅ He's not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right
- ✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ He's living at home normally with you
- ✅ You're covering all his costs; the council isn't paying anything towards him

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** or **by post using form CH2** at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

2. **You'll need to provide:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may still be eligible but could be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge (you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit)

4. **Payment Schedule:**
   - Payments are normally made every 4 weeks
   - If you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits, you may be eligible for weekly payments

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
